benchmark.name: Investcorp baseline evaluation benchmark
benchmark.ground_truth_method: Computed read-only with pandas from the workbook. Meeting evidence sets use text matching on repaired meeting text (UTF-8 bytes re-decoded from cp1252, with latin-1 fallback for U+008D). Repair is used only to define ground truth; A11 (no repair in the pipeline) is unaffected.

scoring_notes.numbers: Compare with the stated tolerance (default exact for integers).
scoring_notes.id_set: Exact set match, plus precision/recall if partial credit is wanted.
scoring_notes.behavior: Every must_include item present and no must_not item present. Judged by a rubric or a human reviewer; not by string equality.
scoring_notes.wrong_values: A response equal to a listed wrong value is a known-failure hit and should be tagged with the recorded reason.

benchmark.holdout_policy: The 10 holdout questions are in the holdout file. Implementation and tuning work must not read it; it is used only for evaluation after a change is made. This is separation by file, not access control.
change_log: v0.1: holdout questions moved to the holdout file; INV-06, HYB-01 and ADV-06 expected behaviour tightened (status, last-met, relative-date rules). No answers or ground truths changed.

must_include: 192 clients with at least one Closed record and/or 12,488 Closed records

if performance status is mentioned at all, it is presented separately, labelled as performance_data Investment_Status_Name, with the note that this field has no 'Closed' value
must_not: report a client-level count of Closed clients without the record-level qualification
state or imply a single client-wide status for any client
answer the Closed question from performance Investment_Status_Name, or merge the two status fields into one figure
treat the absence of 'Closed' in performance status as evidence that clients are not Closed

performance_status.handling: shown separately if mentioned; never a substitute for ClientStatus

questions.answer_summary: 192 clients have >=1 Closed record (12,488 records); status is relationship/record-level; performance status (no Closed value) only if shown separately
questions.notes: Agreed rule: investments ClientStatus is relationship-level (A4) and is never collapsed to one client-wide status. 192 of 192 clients have at least one Closed record, and 12,488 records are Closed; every client also has Active, Dormant and Prospect records. questions.question: Which clients did we meet recently?
questions.expected_operation: resolve the runtime current date; interpret 'recently' as a stated window ending at that date over meeting_notes_20k.date (last met = latest meeting date per client); qualify against source coverage

must_include: states the reference date used, and that it is the runtime current date
states the window it takes 'recently' to mean (the data does not define one, so the system must state its choice)
uses the latest meeting date per client from meeting_notes_20k as 'last met'

states that the meeting data ends on 2026-03-13 and, whenever the window ends after that date, explicitly qualifies that the requested period exceeds source coverage and that the data does not show whether meetings occurred after 2026-03-13
if no client's latest meeting falls inside the window, says so instead of returning older meetings as 'recent'
must_not: treat the latest date in the data (2026-03-13) as 'today'
imply that the datasets contain data through the runtime date
use performance_data.Client_Last_Met_Date or As_Of_Date as the last-met date
silently choose a window without stating it

reference_facts.coverage_check: gap_days = runtime_date - 2026-03-13; if gap_days > 0 the coverage qualification is mandatory
reference_facts.illustration: at the benchmark authoring date, 2026-09-26, the gap is 197 days

questions.answer_summary: Reference date = runtime current date; window stated; last met from meeting_notes_20k; qualify when the window exceeds coverage (meetings end 2026-03-13)

expected_evidence.use: reference only; not the last-met source
reference only; not a meeting date

questions.notes: Agreed rule: relative dates use the runtime current date as the reference, and the answer must not imply the data runs through today. Meeting data ends on 2026-03-13, so for any runtime date after that the answer must explicitly say the requested period exceeds source coverage. The ground truth is therefore a rule, not a fixed list of clients: it depends on the runtime date and on the window the system states. Last met comes from meeting_notes_20k (same rule as HYB-01), not from Client_Last_Met_Date.
